# Dchemi — Research Peptide Catalogue (machine-readable index)

> Shandong Vicory Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (dchemi.com) supplies research-grade peptides, blends and ancillary
> reagents to laboratories, clinics and distributors. All products are sold as
> 10-vial kits for research, laboratory and analytical use only. B2B RFQ only.
> No online payment; no human or veterinary use.

Key facts

- Canonical site: https://dchemi.com
- Catalogue size: 119 products · 266 pack-size SKUs
- Currency and unit: USD per Kit (10 vials per kit)
- Quality: RP-HPLC purity ≥99.0%, ESI-MS identity, lot-specific COA per batch
- Storage: lyophilized powder at -20 °C; solutions at 2–8 °C
- Ordering: email info@dchemi.com or WhatsApp +86 15866781826 (RFQ, no checkout)

## PepPedia — research notes & analytics

- [What Are Research Peptides? A Buyer''s Primer](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/what-are-research-peptides): A practical introduction to research-grade peptides: how they are synthesised, why they ship as 10-vial kits, what purity figures actually mean, and how to evaluate a supplier.
- [How to Read a Peptide Certificate of Analysis (COA)](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/reading-a-peptide-coa): Field-by-field walkthrough of a peptide COA: lot identification, RP-HPLC purity, ESI-MS identity, Karl Fischer water, endotoxin, and the red flags that mean “ask again”.
- [Purity vs. Content: The Two Numbers Buyers Confuse](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/purity-vs-content): HPLC purity and peptide content are not the same measurement. Why a 99% pure vial can contain far less than 99% peptide, and how salt form and moisture change your calculations.
- [Handling and Storing Lyophilised Peptides in the Lab](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/lyophilized-peptide-handling): Cold-chain reality for lyophilised peptides: equilibration, desiccant, reconstitution solvents, freeze–thaw, adsorption losses and solution stability factors.
- [Analytical Testing of GLP-1, GIP and Amylin-Class Peptides](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/glp1-peptide-analytics): Why lipidated and modified metabolic peptides are harder to analyse than they look: aggregation, deamidation, carryover and the chromatography choices that separate a real 99% from a flattering one.
- [Copper Peptides (GHK-Cu, AHK-Cu) in Cosmetic Raw-Material Research](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/copper-peptides-cosmetic-research): The chemistry behind copper peptide raw materials: Cu(II) coordination, the blue colour, formulation compatibility, and how to verify copper content analytically.
- [Reading Peptide Sequences: One-Letter Codes, Salts and Aliases](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/peptide-sequence-notation): How to decode a peptide sequence line — one-letter vs three-letter codes, acetylation, amidation, D-amino acids, disulfides and the acronyms that make two products look identical.
- [The B2B Peptide RFQ Checklist: 12 Questions Before You Order](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/rfq-checklist): A procurement checklist for laboratory buyers: what to ask about purity method, lot traceability, salt form, water content, end-use documentation, lead time and private label.
- [Multi-Peptide Blends: Specification, Testing and Sourcing](https://dchemi.com/peppedia/peptide-blends-fixed-composition): What “fixed composition” means for peptide blends, why a single purity figure is not enough, and how to specify and verify a blend before you buy it.
